title: SEER — Sustainable Electricity Expansion Roadmaps
summary: Democratizing power systems planning for a robust and sustainable energy transition.
overview: Power system planning shapes investments in generation and grid infrastructure. Fragmented data and inaccessible tools can limit participation in these decisions, particularly in the Global South. SEER aims to make planning faster, more flexible, and more accessible to energy-sector stakeholders.

The project is developing an open dataset to support machine learning approaches, including automated input-data generation and models that approximate optimization solvers. Collaboration with planning practitioners is central to making the tools useful for real decisions.

title: The role of electric boiling in the electric cooking transition in Nairobi and Kigali
summary: Investigating the role of electric boiling in the electric cooking transition in Nairobi and Kigali
overview: Investigating the role of electric boiling in the electric cooking transition in Nairobi and Kigali.

In Summer 2025, Eliane Nirere led data collection in Kigali to assess household electricity and cooking-fuel use. She designed the KoboToolbox survey, trained 20 enumerators, and led fieldwork with more than 2,000 households across six sectors. She also led household selection and the distribution of more than 350 kettles to low-electricity-consuming households to assess electric water boiling as a convenient, affordable alternative for cooking tasks.

title: CORE — Community Owned Renewable Electrification
summary: Research and collaboration on community-owned renewable electrification in Nigeria.
overview: The Community-Owned Renewable Electrification (CORE) project supported Nigeria’s Rural Electrification Agency (REA) to develop, test, and scale a community-led model for renewable electricity service provision. Through this model, known as the Renewable Energy Users’ Cooperative Societies (REUCS), communities took ownership of mini-grid operations, governance, and long-term sustainability.

CORE was implemented by a consortium led by Mercy Corps – Energy 4 Impact, together with local partner Murty International and the Kigali Collaborative Research Centre (KCRC). The consortium brought together complementary expertise to strengthen and expand the REUCS model nationwide.

title: Beyond Regional Boundaries: Economic Sector-Specific Energy Transition Typologies for the Global South
summary: Developing research investigating economic and environmental heterogeneity within economic sectors in Global South countries, beginning in Winter 2026.
overview: This project aims to classify Global South countries into distinct sector-specific transition typologies that reflect the development magnitudes and trajectories based on energy usage, economic structures, and environmental impacts across the agriculture, buildings, industry, power and energy, and transportation economic sectors

title: Spotlight Kampala
summary: Community-engaged research on electricity access, service quality, and electric cooking in Kampala’s informal settlements.
overview: Spotlight Kampala brings Ugandan and international researchers together with residents to understand and improve electricity services in informal settlements. Its research connects infrastructure, affordability, safety, and community priorities.

The collaboration surveyed 500 households, conducted 66 interviews, deployed 148 remote power-quality sensors, and mapped infrastructure across 25 communities. Findings were returned to participating communities to help identify priority solutions.

Electric cooking research combines household engagement, monitoring, and wiring inspections. More recent work explores community-designed solar cooking systems and payment, ownership, and maintenance arrangements.

title: Community Benefit Agreements in Utility-Scale Energy Projects
summary: Community Benefit Agreements in Utility-Scale Energy Projects.
overview: Community Benefit Agreements in Utility-Scale Energy Projects.
objectives: Compile U.S. case studies of community benefit agreements (CBAs) for utility-scale energy projects across rural, urban, and tribal communities.
Compare agreement structures, negotiating parties, and terms, with emphasis on how benefits are defined and enforced through responsibilities, reporting, and penalties for non-compliance.
Identify best practices for early, transparent engagement, inclusive decision-making, community priorities, and accountability.
Examine barriers to negotiation and implementation, including trust, information gaps, confidentiality, power imbalances, and enforcement.
Document state and federal policies that encourage or require community benefits, including the Department of Energy’s Community Benefits Plan requirement.
